sentenceSets.sentence: His peripatetic existence made long-term commitments difficult, which was either the cause or the consequence of his restlessness.

answerChoices.reasoning: Transient means short-lived and soon over, but this way of living lasted long enough to shape a whole pattern of commitments and to be bound up with a standing trait of his character.
Erratic points to unpredictability, and what the sentence says obstructs commitment is the shape of his existence over time rather than any inconsistency in his behavior.
Solitude would explain the absence of ties directly, whereas the sentence makes the difficulty a consequence of how he lived and links it to restlessness rather than to being alone.
Nomadism describes a whole people moving together with their herds and their households, while the sentence concerns one man and the commitments he could not keep.
Precariousness is insecurity of footing, and nothing in the sentence suggests his position was fragile, only that it would not stay still.
Improvisation is about doing things without preparation, which does not connect to the long-term commitments the sentence says he could not make.
Secrecy would be a strange reason for commitments to fail and has no link to the restlessness the sentence names.
Frenetic describes a frantic pace, but the obstacle here is duration rather than speed: nothing of his lasted long enough.
Staying put would make long-term commitments easier rather than harder.
Being rooted is the direct opposite of the restlessness the sentence attaches to his way of living.
Monastic life is defined by stability in one house under one rule, which contradicts the difficulty described.

sentenceSets.sentence: The professor was famously peripatetic, conducting entire seminars while leading his students on long loops around the quadrangle.

answerChoices.reasoning: Energy would show in his manner at a lectern just as well, whereas the sentence specifies that the teaching happened while the whole class was on the move outdoors.
Restlessness suggests he could not bear to sit still, but the walking is presented as his settled and celebrated method of holding a seminar.
Digression is wandering in the argument, and what the sentence describes is wandering across actual ground while the argument proceeds.
Informality concerns a relaxed manner, which one can have seated; the defining fact here is the long loops the class covered on foot.
Eccentricity is oddity of any kind and would not tell a reader that the seminars were conducted in motion.
Volubility is a flood of speech, and the sentence's detail is the route around the quadrangle rather than the quantity of talk.
Athleticism implies sport and physical prowess, while the walking here is a way of teaching rather than an exercise.
Socratic names a method of questioning, which says nothing about whether the class stayed in a room.
A man confined to bed could not lead students on loops around a quadrangle.
Immobility contradicts the long walks the seminars are said to consist of.
A recluse avoids company, but this professor teaches whole seminars in the open with his students around him.

sentenceSets.sentence: Her peripatetic first decade as a conductor took her to nineteen orchestras in eleven countries before any permanent post was offered.

answerChoices.reasoning: Prolific counts how much someone produces, while the figures in this sentence count places she went and end with the offer of somewhere to stay.
Meteoric describes a swift rise in standing, but nineteen orchestras in eleven countries measures movement across the map rather than ascent up a ladder.
Rootlessness implies she belonged nowhere and to no one, whereas the sentence is about a run of professional engagements that ends with her accepting a permanent post.
Exhausting reports how the decade felt, and the sentence's numbers report where she was, which is what the contrast with a permanent post depends on.
Freelance describes her contractual status, which would not by itself require nineteen different orchestras in eleven countries.
Provincial implies confinement to the margins, contradicted by a decade spanning eleven countries.
Fame would explain invitations but not the emphasis on how long it took before anywhere offered her a permanent place.
Improvisation concerns how she made music, and the sentence counts only the orchestras and countries she passed through.
Standing still is impossible for someone who worked with nineteen orchestras across eleven countries.
Staying at home is contradicted by the eleven countries the sentence counts.
Remaining in one place is the very thing she is described as finally being offered at the end of the decade.
